label: input token b in the original phase (not at step 0)
explanation: Fires exactly when the letter b is input during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at any position except the first step (t >= 1). On the dev split this matches perfectly: precision, recall and F1 all 1.0. It never fires on b at t = 0, on the <DEL> step, or anywhere in the copy phase, including when b is fed back as input or is the token being output. It never fires on any other input token either. Magnitude depends on position: it is weakest at t = 1 (about 0.3-0.4 of max), strongest at t = 2-4, and falls off again at later positions (t = 7-8 is about 0.4 of max). A repeated b, where an earlier b was already seen, tends to be weaker (about 0.77-0.79 of max versus 0.98 for the first b). Previous token, first token and L have little effect.

issues: None of the checks broke the label. On the test split the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 1.0, F1 1.0 and mass recall 1.0 (90611 active steps, 90611 predicted), with coverage 1.0 in every activation quartile.
misses with --split test found 0 missed activations and 0 false positives, so there is no systematic counterexample class.

The dev profile confirms the factual claims. The feature never fires on the <DEL> step or anywhere in the copy phase, including when b is the output token. It never fires at t=0. Among input tokens it fires only on b. Previous token, first token and L show flat rates.

The magnitude claims fit the per-t activation mass. Mass per active step at t=1 is about half of t=2-3, and later positions taper off. Top examples show a repeated b at about 0.77-0.79 of max after a first b at 0.98. A b at t=1 right after a b at t=0 is about 0.30.
Minor: the explanation calls t=2-4 the strongest positions, but the profile only clearly supports t=2-3. Magnitude is a secondary claim and does not affect the label.

Not a problem with the feature: my own check using n_seen(["b"]) was invalid because I passed strings where the helper expects token indices. The test with prev_tok==b showed the feature also fires on repeated b's (recall share 0.03, precision 1.0).
